picks.what: A street from a height, photograph (Bain News Service, Library of Congress)
picks.why: sharp elevated view down a busy street of wooden and brick houses; negative border and caption trimmed

gaps: P0–P3: nothing; P4: only a close-up of the synagogue front (#3) and a small Orda drawing of a manor house (#4); P6: existing 2016 view kept
notes: #5 is a street scene, not a general view, though taken from a height; despite its title it shows the street, not a group of refugees. Commons dates it only to the 1920s; the refugee subject suggests about 1920. #7 (a street, October 1941, sharp) is an alternate for P5 but the location is unidentified. #1 is the same postcard as #3 with a wrong 1815 date. #6 (garrison church) and #9 (railway station) are single buildings; #8 is a map; #10 a satellite photo; #11 a night street scene, not better than the existing view.
